Create a Piper Plot

Source: R/plot_piper.R
piper_plot.Rd

Create a Piper Plot

Usage

piper_plot(
  samples,
  group = "location_id",
  legend_position = c(0.9, 0.8),
  legend_title = group,
  qc_valid_only = TRUE,
  qc_omit_outliers = TRUE,
  qc_with_alkalinity = TRUE,
  point_colour = "viridis",
  point_shape = 16,
  point_size = 3,
  margin = 10,
  scale = 1
)

Arguments

samples

Data frame. Output from fmt_minimal() or fetch_renmods(). If fetch_renmods() samples will be first formatted with fmt_minimal().

group

Character. Column by which to group data for colour, shape, filled and size.

legend_position

Character or Numeric. Location of legend passed to legend.position argument of ggplot2::theme(). One of none", "left", "right", "bottom", "top", "inside", OR a vector of two numeric values x, and y to specify an exact position.

legend_title

Character. Title of legend. Defaults to group.

qc_omit_outliers

Logical. Whether to omit outliers by looking at dominant water types (see ?dominant_water_types()). Default TRUE.

qc_with_alkalinity

Logical. Whether to use Alkalinity (alkalinity_total_4.5_as_caco3_meq/l) for HCO3 (bicarbonate_alkalinity_as_caco3_meq/l) if HCO3 is missing. Default TRUE. Matches behaviour of water_type().

point_colour

Character. Colour or colours by which to colour points. Either a single value (applied to all), or a vector of values the same length as the number of groups. Can also be "viridis", which will use the viridis colour scale.

point_shape

Numeric. Shape of points to use, 1 - 25, see ?ggplot2::scale_shape(). Either a single value (applied to all), or a vector of values the same length as the number of groups.

margin

Numeric. Plot margin size in "pt". See ggplot2::margin().

scale

Numeric. Scale text (axes titles and tick labels).

qc_valid

Logical. Keep only valid data (charge balances <=10)

Value

ggplot Piper Plot

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
s <- fetch_renmods(ems_ids = "E208101", date_range = c("2001-01-01", "2015-01-01"))
piper_plot(s)

ss <- fmt_minimal(s)
piper_plot(ss)
}
